The argument started with the position that artificial intelligence is good for society. The support for this view was that AI can make everyday life more enjoyable and convenient, which in turn can improve our health and standard of living. However, this first argument was overruled.

An objection was then raised: AI harms the economic well-being of many people and businesses, so AI is not good for society. This challenge was followed by another main argument against AI, namely that AI repeats and exacerbates racism, which hurts racial minorities and therefore makes AI not good for society. This anti-AI argument was justified and remained standing.

In response to the debate, the pro-AI side had not successfully defeated the concerns about economic harm and racial bias. So, based on the argumentation as it stands, the conclusion is that AI is not clearly shown to be good for society overall. The strongest accepted argument in the exchange points to serious social harms, especially for economic well-being and racial minorities.
